title: Cache Telemetry v2 – Rollout Plan (working doc)
content:
Last updated: 2025-02-24 (Connor O’Brien)
Status: working draft for staged enablement across Hosted/Dedicated/Private

Quick links
- Linear umbrella: ENG-4812 (Cache hit-rate instrumentation sprint)
- Pipeline/schema update: ENG-4815
- Gateway attribution: ENG-4816
- Dashboards + alerts: ENG-4817
- Docs/migration notes: ENG-4820
- Runtime hooks PR: redwood/pr-18421
- Runtime structured event + classification PR: redwood/pr-18452
- Gateway tags PR: redwood/pr-18461
- Cardinality guardrails PR: redwood/pr-18475
- Dashboards/alerts pack: observability-pack/pr-921
- Perf canary scenario: perf-canary/pr-233

1) Purpose
We are rolling out KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 across the runtime + gateway + telemetry pipeline to provide trustworthy cache hit-rate and savings metrics (hit-bytes, saved_prefill_ms, cacheable prompt ratio) without blowing up cardinality.

This doc is the staged rollout plan: feature flag names, enablement stages, validation checklists, comms/sign-off, and rollback criteria.

2) Scope / non-goals
In scope
- Runtime emits v2 cache events/counters with per-request outcome classification (hit/miss/partial) behind flags.
- Gateway/control-plane attaches attribution fields (tenant, route, model, region, deployment_mode) with bounded cardinality behavior.
- Telemetry pipeline accepts v2 schema and enforces ADR-027 tag cardinality budget (drop/aggregate rules).
- Dashboards/alerts (new panels) are validated before widening rollout.

Non-goals
- Changing cache algorithm behavior.
- Full customer-facing UI polish for recommendations (Optimize workstream continues separately).
- Backfilling historic data beyond the agreed window (see §7.3).

3) Rollout principles
- “No silent breakage”: instrumentation can be enabled while keeping existing v1 metrics intact until we cut over dashboards/alerts.
- “Bounded blast radius”: start with internal + low-traffic canaries and only then expand by region/tier.
- “Prefer disabling over reverting”: first-line rollback is flipping flags off (runtime + gateway). PR reverts are last resort.
- “Cardinality is a reliability issue”: if tag explosion is detected, we treat as incident-adjacent and roll back.

4) Dependencies / gating items
Must be true before Stage 1 (internal canary)
- Runtime PRs merged and deployed to at least one canary runtime train:
  - redwood/pr-18421 (lookup/insert/evict counters + request correlation)
  - redwood/pr-18452 (cache outcome classification + structured event payload)
- Pipeline schema supports v2 fields and guardrails are active:
  - redwood/pr-18475 (drop/aggregate rules, dashboards-friendly fields)
- Gateway attribution merged and deployed to the same environment(s):
  - redwood/pr-18461
- Basic dashboards in place (can be “engineering only”, not customer-facing):
  - observability-pack/pr-921
- Perf impact validated in at least one representative workload:
  - perf-canary/pr-233 integrated OR manual profiling sign-off from Marcus Reed

Must be true before Stage 3 (wider Hosted)
- Data quality runbook updated and oncall owners aligned (Rafael/Sean).
- Alert noise budget accepted (SRE sign-off; see §8).

5) Feature flags (proposed names; final names should match implementation)
5.1 Runtime flags (serving runtime)
Owner: Omar El-Sayed (implementation), Connor O’Brien (rollout coordination)
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_enabled
  - Default: false
  - Effect: Enables v2 cache metrics emission (counters/events). Does not change caching behavior.
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_emit_events
  - Default: false
  - Effect: Enables structured event payload export (higher volume than pure counters; keep off until pipeline validated).
- runtime.cache_telemetry_saved_prefill_ms
  - Default: false
  - Effect: Enables saved_prefill_ms estimation (CPU-side compute; validate overhead).
- runtime.cache_telemetry_sampling_rate
  - Default: 0.0
  - Effect: Sampling for event-style telemetry (NOT counters). Set per stage.

5.2 Gateway/control-plane flags
Owner: Ethan Park / Amara Diallo
- gateway.cache_telemetry_attach_attribution
  - Default: false
  - Effect: Adds route/model/version/region/deployment_mode and bounded tenant identifiers to cache telemetry.
- gateway.cache_telemetry_attribution_mode
  - Values: strict | compat
  - Default: compat
  - Effect: compat tolerates older runtimes missing certain fields; strict enforces required tags and may drop malformed events.

5.3 Pipeline flags / controls
Owner: Caleb Johnson / Nadia Rahman
- telemetry.cache_v2_schema_accept
  - Default: false (in prod) until Stage 1
  - Effect: Allows ingestion of v2 event payloads/fields.
- telemetry.cache_v2_cardinality_guardrails
  - Default: true in canary, then prod before enabling gateway attachment broadly
  - Effect: Drops/aggregates beyond cardinality budget (ADR-027).
- telemetry.cache_v2_event_aggregation_enabled
  - Default: false until event volume verified
  - Effect: Enables rollups to dashboards-friendly aggregates.

Notes
- We should treat any flag that increases event volume (emit_events, sampling_rate) as separately staged from base counters.
- For Private deployments, flags may be surfaced differently (customer-managed). We need explicit compat behavior and documentation.

6) Enablement stages
We’re rolling out in stages. Each stage has: target scope, required flag settings, success criteria, and timebox.

Stage 0: Dev + staging smoke tests
Scope
- Dev environments + staging clusters only.
Flags
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_enabled=true
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_emit_events=true (sampling_rate <= 0.01)
- gateway.cache_telemetry_attach_attribution=true
- telemetry.cache_v2_schema_accept=true
- telemetry.cache_v2_cardinality_guardrails=true
Success criteria
- v2 metrics/events present end-to-end in staging dashboards.
- No obvious tag explosion warnings.
- Saved_prefill_ms values within sanity bounds (>=0; correlates with hit outcomes).
Timebox
- 1–2 days.

Stage 1: Internal canary (Hosted, single region)
Scope
- Hosted only, one low-traffic region (suggest: us-west-2 canary runtime train).
Flags
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_enabled=true
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_emit_events=false (start with counters only)
- gateway.cache_telemetry_attach_attribution=true
- gateway.cache_telemetry_attribution_mode=compat
- telemetry.cache_v2_schema_accept=true
- telemetry.cache_v2_cardinality_guardrails=true
Success criteria (48h)
- Counters show stable ingestion; no sustained drops in telemetry pipeline throughput.
- Dashboards show plausible hit-rate and cacheable prompt ratio; no “all unknown” attribution buckets.
- No runtime perf regression >1% p95 latency on cache-heavy canary scenario.
Timebox
- 2 days minimum (include one peak period).

Stage 2: Hosted canary expansion (2–3 regions, still counters-only)
Scope
- Hosted: expand to 2–3 regions (e.g., us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1) for tier-limited tenants.
Flags
- Same as Stage 1.
- Optionally enable runtime.cache_telemetry_saved_prefill_ms=true for a subset if overhead is acceptable.
Success criteria (3–5 days)
- Attribution breakdown by route/model looks consistent with known traffic patterns.
- Saved_prefill_ms (if enabled) correlates with prefill latency changes and does not exceed prefill latency baseline.
- Cardinality guardrail drop rate <0.1% of events (target) and not increasing day-over-day.
Timebox
- 1 work week.

Stage 3: Hosted broad enablement (counters + limited events)
Scope
- Hosted: all regions, all tiers.
- Start emitting structured events at low sampling for evidence/debug/recommendation prototyping.
Flags
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_enabled=true (all)
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_emit_events=true with runtime.cache_telemetry_sampling_rate=0.001 initially
- gateway.cache_telemetry_attach_attribution=true
- telemetry.cache_v2_event_aggregation_enabled=true
Success criteria (1–2 weeks)
- Event volume within budget; pipeline latency/lag within SLO.
- Recommendation prototype has enough data (sampled) to generate top offenders without biasing toward specific routes.
- Dashboards and alerts are “trustworthy enough” to share internally as source of truth.

Stage 4: Dedicated (early adopters)
Scope
- Dedicated customers opted-in via account-level config. Start with 1–2 design partners.
Flags
- Same as Stage 3 but sampling_rate may be higher (0.005) if dedicated pipeline capacity allows.
- Ensure tenant attribution uses allowed hashed/ID fields per ADR-027.
Success criteria
- Customer-facing dashboards not required, but internal support readiness required.
- No cross-tenant attribution leakage; verify via synthetic tests + spot checks.
Notes
- Dedicated traffic is often “spiky”; validate that alerts don’t page on expected workload shifts.

Stage 5: Private (VPC / on-prem)
Scope
- Private: staged based on release trains and customer upgrade cycles.
Flags
- Provide default OFF; document enablement steps in private operator docs.
- gateway/cache attribution fields must remain within compat constraints for older runtimes.
Success criteria
- Clear operator guidance; data quality runbook includes private-specific checks (local collectors, egress restrictions, metric drop symptoms).

7) Validation checklists
7.1 Data correctness (must pass before widening scope)
- Hit-rate definition matches spec: hit/miss/partial classification consistent across runtime versions.
- hit_bytes is non-negative and consistent with token counts / expected prefix sizes.
- saved_prefill_ms is:
  - >= 0
  - present only when telemetry_saved_prefill_ms enabled
  - not present (or 0) for misses
  - within reasonable range vs observed prefill latency
- cacheable prompt ratio behaves as expected when prompt normalization is applied in a test workload.
- Compare v1 vs v2 (where overlapping) for directional consistency; v2 may differ but should be explainable.

7.2 Cardinality and tagging health
- Top tag dimensions stable and within budget (ADR-027):
  - tenant (hashed/bucketed where applicable)
  - route
  - model + model_version (or pinned version)
  - region
  - deployment_mode
- Monitor “other/overflow” bucket rates after guardrails.
- Ensure request_id is NOT attached as a tag in prod metrics. If present in events, confirm it’s not being promoted to metric tags by downstream transforms.

7.3 Pipeline health / backfill expectations
- Ingestion lag: confirm event/metric arrival within expected window (document current baseline).
- Aggregations: verify rollups match raw counters (within expected sampling differences).
- Backfill: for dashboards, we will backfill v2 aggregates starting from Stage 1 date forward (no retroactive backfill prior to initial enablement). If we need a limited retrospective backfill for internal comparison, that is a separate approval.

7.4 Runtime overhead / performance guardrails
- Runtime perf acceptance threshold: <1% overhead at p95 for cache-heavy workloads (ENG-4813 acceptance criterion baseline).
- Monitor CPU overhead (telemetry serialization) and GC/malloc hot spots if emit_events enabled.
- If saved_prefill_ms computation shows measurable overhead, keep it off by default and only enable for targeted sampling.

8) Alerts rollout / oncall readiness
Owner: Sergio Costa (build), Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (sign-off)
- Alerts should not be enabled until Stage 2 is stable.
- Use burn-rate/regression-style thresholds rather than absolute hit-rate values (traffic mix changes will move absolute hit-rate).
- Segment primarily by route and region; avoid tenant-level paging.
- Oncall runbook link must exist and include “disable flags first” steps.

Proposed alert enablement
- Stage A (shadow): alerts compute but do not page; reviewed daily for 3–5 days.
- Stage B (paging in business hours): pages during staffed hours only.
- Stage C (full paging): after noise budget acceptable for 1 week.

9) Rollback criteria and playbooks
We roll back if any of the following trigger:

Category 1: Cardinality/tag explosion
- Symptoms: cardinality_guardrails drop rate sustained >1% OR timeseries count spikes beyond agreed budget OR downstream costs spike unexpectedly.
- Action:
  1) Set gateway.cache_telemetry_attach_attribution=false (fastest cardinality reduction).
  2) If still high, set runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_emit_events=false and sampling_rate=0.
  3) If still high, set runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_enabled=false.
  4) File incident + follow-up: identify offending tag dimension or transform.

Category 2: Pipeline instability / lag
- Symptoms: ingestion lag exceeds SLO for >30 min; dropped events; dashboards showing long gaps.
- Action:
  1) Disable emit_events first (volume lever).
  2) Reduce sampling_rate to 0.
  3) If necessary disable v2 entirely.

Category 3: Runtime perf regression
- Symptoms: >1% p95 latency regression sustained in canary; perf-canary fails gating thresholds.
- Action:
  1) Disable saved_prefill_ms computation.
  2) Disable emit_events.
  3) Disable v2 metrics.
  4) Engage runtime perf owner (Marcus) for profiling; do not widen rollout.

Category 4: Data correctness failure (misleading dashboards)
- Symptoms: hit-rate indicates improvement but latency savings don’t correlate; partial-prefill miscount discovered; inconsistent classification across routes.
- Action:
  1) Freeze widening rollout.
  2) If incorrect data is being used in alerts/recs, disable emit_events and/or disable v2.
  3) Add dashboard annotation: “v2 telemetry under validation” where necessary.

10) Comms plan / change management
- Slack updates
  - eng-platform: rollout status, any flag flips, known issues
  - eng-runtime: perf/correctness issues
  - eng-sre: alert shadow results + paging enablement
  - product (Optimize): availability of v2 evidence fields and sampling levels

- Change log entries
  - Each stage expansion should be noted in release/change log (internal) with date/time/region and owner.

- Customer comms
  - No proactive customer comms until Dedicated early adopters (Stage 4). For Dedicated, CS/support should have a short explanation and expected changes in metrics naming/behavior.

11) Open questions / TODOs
- Finalize exact flag names as implemented (need confirmation from runtime + gateway owners).
- Decide whether model_version is always attached or only when pinned (trade-off: fragmentation vs value).
- Confirm how tenant attribution is represented for Hosted vs Dedicated (hashed tenant bucket vs internal tenant_id) per ADR-027.
- Determine default sampling_rate for events in Hosted broad rollout (0.001 vs 0.0005).
- Confirm whether we want a single global kill switch across runtime/gateway (prefer “emergency disable cache telemetry v2”).

12) Proposed sign-off checklist (who + what)
Before Stage 2 → Stage 3
- Telemetry: Nadia/Caleb sign off that pipeline guardrails stable; drop rate acceptable.
- Runtime: Omar sign off that perf overhead within threshold.
- SRE: Sean/Rafael sign off that dashboards stable enough for internal oncall context.
- Platform: Ethan/Amara sign off that attribution fields are stable and not exploding cardinality.

Before enabling paging alerts
- Sergio validates alert templates + segmentation.
- SRE validates noise budget in shadow mode.

Appendix: Suggested stage schedule (tentative)
- Week 1 (Mon–Tue): Stage 0 in staging
- Week 1 (Wed–Fri): Stage 1 internal canary (counters-only)
- Week 2: Stage 2 regional expansion + saved_prefill_ms subset
- Week 3: Stage 3 broad Hosted + event sampling
- Week 4+: Stage 4 Dedicated early adopters; Stage 5 Private planning with docs

Notes to self (Connor)
- Make sure every stage change has a rollback timestamp/owner written down.
- Coordinate with Mei Lin on any dashboard backfill assumptions; we should not accidentally chart v1 + v2 as one series.
- Ask Cole Summers to sanity check that saved_prefill_ms / hit_bytes are not accidentally treated as billable usage anywhere in metering transforms.
